item.title: Sudurpashchim Province Assembly member Deuba removed from office
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: Sudurpaschim Province Assembly member and former Minister for Physical Infrastructure Development Prakash Bahadur Deuba has been removed from office. Province Assembly Secretary Dev Bahadur Bogati said Deuba was removed for remaining absent from more than 10 consecutive meetings without prior notice, in accordance with the Constitution of Nepal, 2015, and the Sudurpashchim Province Assembly […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Sudurpaschim Province Assembly member and former Minister for Physical Infrastructure Development Prakash Bahadur Deuba has been removed from office.

Province Assembly Secretary Dev Bahadur Bogati said Deuba was removed for remaining absent from more than 10 consecutive meetings without prior notice, in accordance with the Constitution of Nepal, 2015, and the Sudurpashchim Province Assembly Rules.

He said Speaker Bhim Bahadur Bhandari made the decision to remove Deuba on Tuesday.

As per Article 180(d) of the Constitution, a provincial assembly member’s seat becomes vacant if the member remains absent from 10 consecutive meetings without giving notice. The Sudurpaschim Province Assembly Rules also contain a similar provision.

Deuba left for the United States on personal business in the second week of September last year, shortly after the Gen-Z protests. He has not returned to Nepal since.

He was elected to the Sudurpashchim Province Assembly in 2022 from the Kailali-5(B) seat as a Nepali Congress candidate.

Province Chief Nazir Miyan administered the oath to Bhatta at a special ceremony held at the Office of the Province Chief on Friday. Earlier on Friday morning, Province Chief Miyan appointed Bhatta as Chief Minister of Sudurpaschim Province. […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Newly appointed Sudurpaschim Province Chief Minister Khagaraj Bhatta has taken the oath of office and secrecy.

Province Chief Nazir Miyan administered the oath to Bhatta at a special ceremony held at the Office of the Province Chief on Friday.

Earlier on Friday morning, Province Chief Miyan appointed Bhatta as Chief Minister of Sudurpaschim Province. Bhatta had reached the Province Chief’s Office and staked his claim to form the provincial government.

His claim was backed by Rajendra Singh Rawal, leader of the CPN-UML parliamentary party in the province assembly.

Bhatta replaces Kamal Bahadur Shah of Nepali Congress, who stepped down on Thursday after it became certain that he would not pass the floor test following the withdrawal of support by coalition partner UML.

item.content:encoded:
BAJURA: One person is missing and two others have been injured after a landslide buried houses in Tamsu of Triveni Municipality-9 in Bajura district following incessant rainfall.

The landslide buried the houses of local residents Dharma Thapa, 39, and Karn Bahadur Thapa, 43, after heavy rain began falling continuously last night.

According to Police Inspector Naresh Bahadur Shahi, information officer at the District Police Office, two people were injured when the houses were buried by the landslide.

Nanda Thapa, ward chair of Triveni Municipality-9, said continuous rainfall has made it difficult to rescue the injured and search for the missing person.

Following the incident, a 17-member team led by Deputy Superintendent of Police Shaileshwori Bohara, chief of the District Police Office, has headed to the site with necessary rescue equipment.

item.title: Sudurpashchim Chief Minister Kamal Bahadur Shah resigns
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: Sudurpashchim Province Chief Minister Kamal Bahadur Shah has tendered his resignation. Shah announced his resignation while addressing a meeting of the Sudurpashchim Provincial Assembly on Thursday after failing to secure a majority to save his government. His resignation came on the final constitutional deadline to seek a vote of confidence. The coalition government led […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Sudurpashchim Province Chief Minister Kamal Bahadur Shah has tendered his resignation.

Shah announced his resignation while addressing a meeting of the Sudurpashchim Provincial Assembly on Thursday after failing to secure a majority to save his government. His resignation came on the final constitutional deadline to seek a vote of confidence.

The coalition government led by Shah, a Nepali Congress (NC) leader, fell into a minority after coalition partner CPN-UML withdrew its support on July 15. Under Article 188 (2) of the Constitution of Nepal, 2015, Shah was required to table a motion for a vote of confidence within 30 days. That 30-day constitutional deadline expired on Thursday.

The UML walked out of the government and withdrew its support after the NC decided to end its partnership with the UML in July. The two parties had originally formed an alliance in July 2024 to lead governments across all seven provinces.

Following the collapse of the NC-UML coalition, the UML worked out a new power-sharing arrangement with the Nepali Communist Party (NCP). Under the agreement, the NCP is set to form governments in Sudurpashchim and Karnali Provinces, while the UML will lead governments in Koshi, Bagmati, and Lumbini Provinces.

After completing his address in the provincial assembly, Shah submitted his resignation letter to Province Chief Nazir Miya. His resignation has paved the way for the new UML-NCP alliance to form a new government in Sudurpashchim.

item.title: Sudurpashchim Chief Minister Shah preparing to step down
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: Sudurpaschim Province Chief Minister Kamal Bahadur Shah, who was preparing to seek a vote of confidence after the withdrawal of support by coalition partner CPN-UML, is preparing to step down. He could resign on Tuesday or Wednesday, sources close to Shah say. Shah decided to step down after it became clear he would not […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Sudurpaschim Province Chief Minister Kamal Bahadur Shah, who was preparing to seek a vote of confidence after the withdrawal of support by coalition partner CPN-UML, is preparing to step down.

He could resign on Tuesday or Wednesday, sources close to Shah say.

Shah decided to step down after it became clear he would not secure the required majority in the provincial assembly to win a vote of confidence.

The Nepali Congress (NC) parliamentary party leader is currently serving his second term as Sudurpashchim Chief Minister. He earlier held the office from February 10, 2023 to April 4, 2024. He returned to office for the second term on August 5, following a short four-month stint of Dirgha Bahadur Sodari of CPN (Unified Socialist).

The Unified Socialist has now merged with the CPN (Maoist Center) to form the NCP.

Support from 27 lawmakers is needed for a majority in the 53-member Sudurpashchim Province Assembly.

The new coalition of UML and Nepali Communist Party enjoys a comfortable majority in the province assembly. NCP is the largest party in the province assembly with 22 members, while UML has 11.

Shah’s resignation will pave the way for the UML-NCP alliance to form a government in Sudurpashchim. As per the agreement between the two parties, the NCP will lead the government.

According to a statement issued by the Nepali Army, three women and two men have been taken to Nepalgunj Medical College. Likewise, two male patients, whose […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: A Nepali Army chopper airlifted five people, who were seriously injured in a jeep accident in Sugure of Bajhang on Saturday, to Nepalgunj for further treatment on Sunday.

According to a statement issued by the Nepali Army, three women and two men have been taken to Nepalgunj Medical College.

Likewise, two male patients, whose condition was more critical, were airlifted to Surkhet by a Nepali Army helicopter and then flown to Kathmandu aboard a Sky Truck aircraft for advanced treatment.

Another young girl requiring medical care was also transported to Surkhet Provincial Hospital during the same operation, according ot the army.

Three people were killed and seven others were injured when the jeep crashed in Sugure of Kedarsyun Rural Municipality-7, Bajhang, on Saturday.

item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: One person was killed and 10 others injured when a passenger bus met with an accident in Baitadi on Friday evening.

The accident occurred along the Dasharathchand Highway at Sailek in Dasharathchand Municipality-4.

According to the Armed Police Force (APF) Nepal, the deceased has been identified as Birendra Bahadur Chand (35) of Dasharathchand Municipality-6.

Five of the injured are reported to be in critical condition. The injured have been sent to Baitadi District Hospital for further treatment.

DSP Sahilendra Thapa, joint spokesperson for the APF Nepal, said the bus travelling from Dhangadhi to Baitadi went out of control and plunged about 30 metres off the road.

A joint team from the APF Nepal, Nepal Army and Nepal Police was deployed for rescue operations.

item.title: NC changes three ministers, two state ministers in Sudurpashchim
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: Sudurpashchim Chief Minister Kamal Bahadur Shah reshuffled his cabinet on Monday, inducting three new ministers and two state ministers. Province Chief Nazir Miyan appointed Bel Bahadur Rana Magar as Minister for Social Development, Bikram Singh Dhami as Minister for Economic Affairs, and Man Bahadur Rawal as Minister for Industry, Tourism, Forests and Environment on […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: Sudurpashchim Chief Minister Kamal Bahadur Shah reshuffled his cabinet on Monday, inducting three new ministers and two state ministers.

Province Chief Nazir Miyan appointed Bel Bahadur Rana Magar as Minister for Social Development, Bikram Singh Dhami as Minister for Economic Affairs, and Man Bahadur Rawal as Minister for Industry, Tourism, Forests and Environment on the recommendation of Chief Minister Shah.

Miyan administered the oath of office and secrecy to the new ministers on Monday.

Likewise, Madhu Bharati has been appointed as Minister of State for Social Development and Juna Dani as Minister of State for Economic Affairs. Chief Minister Shah administered the oath of office to the two state ministers.

These five replace Bal Bahadur Singh Thapa, Megh Raj Khadka, Shiva Raj Bhatta, Prakash Bam and Saraswati Khadka from Shah’s cabinet.

Chief Minister Shah, who is from NC, is leading a coalition government of NC and CPN-UML.

All three ministers and two state ministers are from the NC. Although there were demands within UML to change its ministers as well, UML leadership is yet to make any decision in this direction.

A meeting chaired by Minister for Land Management, Cooperatives and Poverty Alleviation Pratibha Rawal on Sunday decided to form the committee led by Deputy Director General of the Department of Survey Sushil Dangol. […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The government has formed a committee to study the technical aspects of the ongoing border dispute between Bajura and Humla districts.

A meeting chaired by Minister for Land Management, Cooperatives and Poverty Alleviation Pratibha Rawal on Sunday decided to form the committee led by Deputy Director General of the Department of Survey Sushil Dangol. The committee will have one representative each from the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, and the Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives and Poverty Alleviation. Likewise, representatives from the Offices of the Chief Ministers and Council of Ministers of Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces are also in the committee. A director of the Department of Survey will serve as the member secretary.

The committee has been tasked with submitting a report to the ministry after studying the technical aspects of the border dispute between the two districts. People from both districts are claiming the pastureland and the trail to Saipal Himal Base Camp at Ranikharka/Ranisain beyond Lampata as their own.

The meeting was attended by Land Management and Cooperative Secretary Madan Bhujel, Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s press and research expert Deepa Dahal; Home Ministry Joint Secretary Anand Kafle; Land Management Ministry Prakash Dahal, Department of Survey Director General Prakash Joshi, Land Management Ministry Under Secretary Bhim Budha; Department of Survey Director Dayanand Joshi, and Survey Officer Jyoti Dhakal.

item.title: Japan, UNDP launch climate resilience project in Dhangadhi
item.dc:creator: bishnu
item.description: KATHMANDU: The Government of Japan and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) have launched a $1.296 million project aimed at strengthening urban resilience to climate risks in Dhangadhi Sub-Metropolitan City. The initiative, titled “Smart Buildings and Green Infrastructure for Improved Human Security and Sustainable Development,” is part of UNDP’s global Climate Promise programme. It focuses […]
item.content:encoded:
KATHMANDU: The Government of Japan and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) have launched a $1.296 million project aimed at strengthening urban resilience to climate risks in Dhangadhi Sub-Metropolitan City.

The initiative, titled “Smart Buildings and Green Infrastructure for Improved Human Security and Sustainable Development,” is part of UNDP’s global Climate Promise programme. It focuses on addressing rising heat risks and promoting sustainable urban development.

The project was launched in Kathmandu by Japanese Ambassador to Nepal Toru Maeda and UNDP Nepal Resident Representative Kyoko Yokosuka, according to a statement issued by the Embassy of Japan in Kathmandu.

“Nepal is warming at nearly twice the global average, with urban areas facing
increasing risks. In Dhangadhi, temperatures frequently exceed 40°C during recurrent heatwaves from May to August,” the embassy said in the statement. “Rapid and unplanned urbanization, shrinking green spaces, and limited energy-efficient infrastructure are intensifying impacts on health, livelihoods, and essential services, particularly for low-income households and outdoor workers.”

Speaking at the event, Ambassador Maeda reaffirmed Japan’s commitment to supporting climate resilience in Nepal, especially for vulnerable communities. He said the project is expected to enhance the city’s ability to cope with extreme heat through integrated urban heat management solutions.

Similarly, UNDP’s Yokosuka said the project will focus on practical interventions, including thermal retrofitting of public buildings, restoration of urban wetlands, and promotion of nature-based cooling solutions. She added that these approaches are designed to be scalable and replicated in other cities facing similar climate challenges.

The project will combine infrastructure development, urban planning, and local capacity building to address rising heat risks. It is expected to directly benefit around 4,000 people.
